title.en: Kuba raffia: a cloth made by many hands
title.zh: 库巴拉菲草织物：许多双手的作品

location.label: Sankuru region, Kuba textile setting; approximate

labelI18n.en: Sankuru region, Kuba textile setting; approximate
labelI18n.zh: 库巴织物所在的桑库鲁地区；约指

summary.en:
A prestige panel can look like a single design, yet its making depended on several kinds of skill. Kuba men wove a ground cloth from raffia palm fiber; women joined, dyed and decorated the material. In cut-pile panels, embroidered threads were clipped to create a soft surface. The finished pieces could be displayed and used as valuables, while larger assembled cloths became garments.

The Met's double panel, dated from the late nineteenth to the mid twentieth century, sets interlocking shapes slightly out of regular sequence. That variation rewards close looking. Pattern names could remember people or ordinary things, making invention part of tradition. Beside the atlas's Kuba political history, the cloth shows how authority, exchange and artistic skill also took shape inside a collaborative process.
summary.zh:
一块显贵身份织片看似完整图案，制作却依赖多种技艺。库巴男子用拉菲草纤维织底布，女子拼接、染色并装饰。在割绒织片上，刺绣的线被剪开，形成柔软表面。成品可以陈列，也可作为有价值的交换物；更大的拼接布则做成服饰。

大都会博物馆这件双联织片被定于十九世纪晚期至二十世纪中叶，交错形状没有机械地重复，细看才能发现变化。图案名称可以纪念人物，也可以来自日常事物，使创新成为传统的一部分。把它放在库巴政治史旁边，可以看到权威、交换与艺术技艺如何也在共同制作中形成。

dateNote.en: 1875–1950 is an approximate display window for the catalogue’s late nineteenth–mid twentieth-century object date, not the origin or endpoint of Kuba weaving.
dateNote.zh: 1875—1950年为目录“十九世纪晚期至二十世纪中叶”的约略显示区间，不是库巴织造的起止年。

sources.title: Double Prestige Panel, 1999.522.15
sources.evidenceNote: Supports the object date and Sankuru attribution, collaborative production, cut pile, uses and named patterns. The possible borrowing of cut pile through trade is not asserted as established.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 支持器物年代、桑库鲁归属、协作制作、割绒、用途与图案命名；未将可能经贸易传播的技法视为定论。

expansion.sourceReview: Original bilingual synthesis from inspected institutional records, primary documents and specialist research; source-specific claims and limits are retained.

reviewLimit.en: The catalogue does not identify this panel’s individual makers or a precise workshop. Its production sequence is a documented tradition, not a recovered biography of every participant.
reviewLimit.zh: 目录未确定此织片具体制作者或作坊；制作流程是有记录的传统，并非每位参与者的复原生平。

title.en: Mangaaka: carving, ritual and public promises
title.zh: 曼加卡：雕刻、仪式与公共承诺

location.label: Chiloango River region on the Loango coast; approximate

labelI18n.en: Chiloango River region on the Loango coast; approximate
labelI18n.zh: 洛安哥海岸的奇洛安戈河地区；约指

summary.en:
The iron pieces driven into a Mangaaka figure are traces of repeated encounters with a community. Such figures served as witnesses to vows and agreements and as instruments through which specialists addressed disputes. A sculptor made the wooden body; a nganga prepared and installed charged materials, and ritual action gave the assembled work its social role.

The Met's example, dated about 1880–1900, still carries ironwork but has lost parts of its original contents and attachments. Conservation studies compare wood, resins and other substances across related figures. Looking at materials therefore changes the question from “Who carved this?” to “Who helped make and use it?” The object connects Kongo authority with collective practice, while its altered condition reminds us that a museum sculpture is only part of the original ensemble.
summary.zh:
钉入曼加卡像的铁件，留下了群体多次参与的痕迹。这类像见证誓言与约定，也让仪式专家借以处理争端。雕刻者制成木身，恩甘加专家配制、安置具有灵力意义的材料，再通过仪式使整件作品发挥社会作用。

大都会博物馆的此例约作于1880—1900年，仍保留铁件，却已失去部分原有内容物与附件。保护研究通过比较相关作品的木材、树脂等物质，重建制作方式。于是问题从“谁雕刻它”扩展为“谁参与制作和使用它”。这件作品把刚果地区的权威与集体实践相连，其改变后的状态也提醒人们，博物馆中的雕像只是原来组合的一部分。

dateNote.en: About 1880–1900 follows the collection record. The map represents the regional production setting established by conservation research, not a known workshop address.
dateNote.zh: 约1880—1900年依馆藏目录；地图代表保护研究所定的区域制作背景，不是已知作坊地址。

sources.title: Mangaaka Power Figure, 2008.30
sources.evidenceNote: The catalogue identifies collaborative authorship, c.1880–1900, the social meaning of metal insertions, missing components and a Public Domain image.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 目录确认共同制作、约1880—1900年、铁件的社会含义、缺失部件及公有领域图像。

sources.title: The Materials That Make Mangaaka
sources.publisher: Ellen Howe and Adriana Rizzo, The Metropolitan Museum of Art
sources.evidenceNote: Conservation research places production in the Chiloango region and examines multiple woods, resins and packed materials; no single disputed botanical identification is generalized to all figures.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 保护研究将制作定位于奇洛安戈地区，考察多种木材、树脂与填充物；不把有争议的植物鉴定推广到所有作品。

expansion.sourceReview: Original bilingual synthesis from inspected institutional records, primary documents and specialist research; source-specific claims and limits are retained.

reviewLimit.en: Ritual meanings are presented as the participants’ practices and beliefs. No individual vow or treaty is assigned to an unidentified nail.
reviewLimit.zh: 仪式含义作为参与者的实践与信仰呈现，不把某枚未识别铁钉对应到具体誓言或条约。

title.en: Olowe of Ise: a palace doorway stages an encounter
title.zh: 伊塞的奥洛韦：宫门上的相遇

labelI18n.zh: 尼日利亚埃基蒂地区伊塞

summary.en:
A doorway could turn a visitor's arrival into a lasting political scene. Around 1904–1910, Olowe of Ise carved a palace portal commemorating the Arinjale of Ise's reception of a British delegation. One side centers the Yoruba ruler; the other shows a European carried in a litter, surrounded by attendants. The artist carved figures at different depths and turned bodies and heads to suggest movement.

The two panels invite comparison: how are rank, service and motion made visible? This was a commission within a living court culture, produced during expanding colonial power. Naming Olowe restores the artist to a history often presented through anonymous “tribal art.” At the same time, the royal commission reveals whose perspective the carved event was designed to preserve.
summary.zh:
一道门可以把来访变成持久的政治场景。约1904—1910年，伊塞的奥洛韦雕刻宫门，纪念伊塞君主阿林贾莱接待英国代表团。一侧以约鲁巴君主为中心，另一侧表现坐在肩舆中的欧洲来客及其随从。雕刻采用不同深度，身体与头部朝向也不相同，由此表现行动。

把两扇门比较起来，可以追问等级、服侍与运动怎样变得可见。这是一项仍在运作的宫廷文化中的委托，完成于殖民权力扩张时期。保留奥洛韦的姓名，让艺术家回到常被泛称为“部族艺术”的历史之中；同时，王室委托也显示，这段相遇原本要保存谁的视角。

dateNote.en: The carving is dated approximately 1904–1910. Catalogues describe the represented reception around the turn of the century; its exact day and year are not assigned here.
dateNote.zh: 雕刻约作于1904—1910年。目录将所表现的接待置于世纪之交前后，此处不指定确切年月日。

sources.title: Palace door, 88-13-1
sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of African Art
sources.evidenceNote: Identifies Olowe, Ise, c.1904–1910, the right panel’s ruler, high-relief technique and the paired reception scene. Image reuse is restricted on this page.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 确认奥洛韦、伊塞、约1904—1910年、右扇君主、高浮雕技法及成对接待场景；此页图像再使用有限制。

sources.title: Ise palace door, 841603
sources.evidenceNote: Identifies the matching left panel, European in a litter, retainers and the Arinjale’s reception of Captain Ambrose’s delegation. The object is on loan and not marked as a downloadable open image.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 确认对应左扇、肩舆中的欧洲人、随从及阿林贾莱接待安布罗斯代表团；作品为借展，未标为可下载开放图像。

expansion.sourceReview: Original bilingual synthesis from inspected institutional records, primary documents and specialist research; source-specific claims and limits are retained.

reviewLimit.en: The carved commemoration is a patron’s representation, not a photograph. It is distinct from Olowe’s Ikere doors later shown at the 1924 British Empire Exhibition.
reviewLimit.zh: 雕刻纪念是委托者的表现方式，并非照片；此件与1924年大英帝国展览中展示的奥洛韦伊凯雷宫门不同。

title.en: Merer’s logbook: moving stone for Khufu’s pyramid
title.zh: 梅勒的日志：为胡夫的金字塔运石

location.label: Giza, destination of Merer’s limestone deliveries

labelI18n.en: Giza, destination of Merer’s limestone deliveries
labelI18n.zh: 梅勒石灰石运输的目的地吉萨

summary.en:
The Great Pyramid required stone to arrive before anyone could set it in place. Papyrus logbooks associated with the inspector Merer record a crew carrying limestone from Tura to Khufu's building project at Giza. Other papers in the same archive account for commodities delivered to workers. The surviving entries make transport, scheduling and provisioning visible within a monument usually encountered as a finished shape.

The papyri were recovered in 2013 at the Red Sea harbor of Wadi el-Jarf, far from the work described in these entries. Their findspot and their subject are different places. Connecting the logbook to the atlas's pyramid and workshop records shifts attention from a king's name to coordinated labor, waterways and records.
summary.zh:
巨石必须先运到工地，才能砌入大金字塔。与监察员梅勒有关的纸草日志，记录一支船队把图拉石灰石运到胡夫在吉萨的工程。同一档案的其他文书核算送给工人的物资。残存记录让运输、日程与供给变得可见，而人们通常只看到已经建成的纪念物。

这些纸草于2013年在红海港口瓦迪杰尔夫出土，远离这些条目所记的工作地点，出土地与记述对象并不是同一处。把日志与图集中的金字塔、工坊故事联系起来，可以从君王姓名转向协同劳动、水路与记录。

dateNote.en: About 2530 BCE is a representative late-Khufu date within the chronology given by the excavator’s museum lecture. The document’s regnal dating is firmer than an exact civil-year conversion.
dateNote.zh: 约前2530年为发掘者博物馆讲座所采用年代框架内的胡夫晚期示意年；文献的王年纪年比精确公元换算更可靠。

sources.title: City of the Pyramids: Wadi el-Jarf and the Journal of Merer
sources.publisher: Pierre Tallet and Mark Lehner, Museum of Fine Arts Boston
sources.evidenceNote: Excavators’ lecture descriptions give the 2013 find, late Khufu context, workers’ provisions and Tura–Giza limestone transport; no direct evidence for stone-lifting machinery is claimed.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 发掘者讲座说明提供2013年发现、胡夫晚期背景、工人物资及图拉至吉萨运石；未声称直接证明石块提升机械。

expansion.sourceReview: Original bilingual synthesis from inspected institutional records, primary documents and specialist research; source-specific claims and limits are retained.

reviewLimit.en: The map marks the documented destination, not the papyrus findspot. No new navigational route, workforce total or universal labor-status claim is inferred.
reviewLimit.zh: 地图标记有据的目的地，而非纸草出土地；不据此新建航行路线、推算工人总数或概括所有劳动者身份。

title.en: Ibadan àdìrẹ: signatures in an indigo market
title.zh: 伊巴丹阿迪雷：靛蓝市场中的署名

location.label: Ibadan, Nigeria, production and purchase setting

labelI18n.en: Ibadan, Nigeria, production and purchase setting
labelI18n.zh: 尼日利亚伊巴丹，制作与购藏地点

summary.en:
A small scorpion-like mark on a cloth's hem can preserve authorship even when a name has been lost. Two hand-painted àdìrẹ cloths collected in Ibadan in the 1960s carry such a signature. Women painted cassava-starch resist onto cotton before indigo dyeing, leaving pale designs when the protected areas were revealed. Other makers tied or stitched the cloth to resist the dye.

Patterns responded to the city and to customers. One celebrated Ibadan through the columns of Mapo Hall; another design was described to collectors as the fashionable cloth of 1964. Imported factory cotton became a material for local invention. These textiles connect Nigeria's political milestones to working knowledge, changing taste and women's businesses. The signature invites recognition of a maker without supplying a name that the collection cannot establish.
summary.zh:
衣边一个像蝎子的标记，即使姓名失传，也可能保存作者身份。二十世纪六十年代在伊巴丹购藏的两件手绘阿迪雷布，带有这样的署名。女子在棉布上涂木薯淀粉防染，再浸入靛蓝，受到保护的部分形成浅色纹样。其他制作者则通过扎结或缝缀防染。

图案回应城市生活与顾客需求。一种用马波市政厅的柱子歌咏伊巴丹；另一种被当地卖家称为1964年的流行布样。进口机制棉布成为本地创新的材料。这些织物把尼日利亚的政治节点与实作知识、品味变化及女子经营联系起来。署名让人看到制作者，却不能补出馆藏尚未确定的姓名。

dateNote.en: Focus: the V&A’s Ibadan cloths from the 1960s, including a design recorded as fashionable in 1964. These are collection dates and fashion evidence, not the beginning of àdìrẹ.
dateNote.zh: 重点为维多利亚与艾尔伯特博物馆的六十年代伊巴丹布样，包括记为1964年流行的一种图案；这些是器物与时尚证据，不是阿迪雷的起源。

sources.title: Àdìrẹ: tied and dyed indigo textiles
sources.evidenceNote: Supports 1960s Ibadan objects, starch/tying/stitching processes, imported cotton, the 1964 design, Mapo Hall pattern and an unidentified scorpion signature. Machine-stitched work is distinguished from women’s hand-painting.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 支持六十年代伊巴丹实物、淀粉与扎缝防染、进口棉布、1964年样式、市政厅图案及姓名未定的蝎形署名；区分男子机缝与女子手绘。

expansion.sourceReview: Original bilingual synthesis from inspected institutional records, primary documents and specialist research; source-specific claims and limits are retained.

reviewLimit.en: The signature is not assigned a personal name. The source describes gendered practices with exceptions; it does not establish that every production stage was always performed by women.
reviewLimit.zh: 不为署名指定个人姓名。资料记述带有例外的性别分工，并不证明所有环节始终只由女子完成。

title.en: Equiano’s book: turning testimony into a public campaign
title.zh: 埃奎亚诺的书：把见证化为公共行动

location.label: London, publication center of Equiano’s autobiography

labelI18n.en: London, publication center of Equiano’s autobiography
labelI18n.zh: 埃奎亚诺自传的出版中心伦敦

summary.en:
Olaudah Equiano, also known as Gustavus Vassa, did more than write a life story. Publishing The Interesting Narrative in 1789 required finding readers willing to subscribe before the book appeared. That support helped him finance publication and retain control over a work sold in his own name. Subscriber lists connected the book to abolitionists, religious networks and public figures.

The title's insistence that it was written by its subject mattered: a formerly enslaved author claimed authority to describe slavery and address the people debating its future. Further editions followed, including a ninth in 1794. Read the book's publication alongside the atlas's slave-trade and emancipation records. Legal change depended in part on people building audiences, making arguments and turning personal testimony into a durable public object.
summary.zh:
奥劳达·埃奎亚诺又名古斯塔夫斯·瓦萨，他不只是写下一段生平。1789年出版《有趣的自述》，需要在书问世之前找到愿意预订的读者。这种支持帮助他筹措出版费用，并掌握以本人名义售卖的作品。预订名单把书与废奴人士、宗教网络和公共人物联系起来。

书名强调“本人所著”具有分量：一位曾被奴役的作者，主张自己有权讲述奴役经历，并向讨论其未来的人发言。此后持续出版新版本，1794年已有第九版。将此书出版与图集中的奴隶贸易及解放法令并读，可以看到法律改变也依赖人们建立读者群、提出论证，并把个人见证变成可以流传的公共作品。

dateNote.en: Focus: the first edition of 1789 through the ninth edition of 1794. No exact birthplace, birth date or reconstructed childhood itinerary is assigned in this publication-focused story.
dateNote.zh: 重点为1789年初版至1794年第九版。本篇聚焦出版，不指定确切出生地、出生年或复原童年行程。

sources.title: The Interesting Narrative: digitized editions
sources.evidenceNote: Lists the 1789 London first edition as printed for and sold by the author and the 1794 ninth edition. Scans are linked to holding libraries.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 列出1789年伦敦初版“为作者印行并由作者销售”，以及1794年第九版，扫描件关联收藏图书馆。

sources.title: Subscribers to the Interesting Narrative
sources.evidenceNote: The Subscribers section explains advance commitments, self-publication, copyright retention and supporters; only the publication evidence is used, not the page’s inconsistent early-life chronology.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: “Subscribers”节说明预订、自行出版、保留版权及支持者；仅采用出版证据，不采用该页有出入的早期生平纪年。

expansion.sourceReview: Original bilingual synthesis from inspected institutional records, primary documents and specialist research; source-specific claims and limits are retained.

reviewLimit.en: Publication history and the author’s political intervention are the focus. Disagreement about birthplace does not require choosing an unsupported African map coordinate.
reviewLimit.zh: 重点是出版史与作者的政治介入；出生地争议不要求选择未经证实的非洲地图坐标。

title.en: Uluburun: a ship carrying unfinished things
title.zh: 乌鲁布伦：装载未成品的船

location.label: Uluburun wreck, off Kaş on the Anatolian coast

labelI18n.en: Uluburun wreck, off Kaş on the Anatolian coast
labelI18n.zh: 安纳托利亚海岸卡什外海的乌鲁布伦沉船

summary.en:
A ship lost off the Anatolian coast carried much more than finished luxuries. Copper and tin ingots traveled beside glass, ivory, amber, resin, foodstuffs and manufactured objects. These materials point toward work still to be done: casting, carving, coloring and preparing goods for use. The cargo makes distant workshops visible as parts of an interconnected economy.

Excavation from 1984 to 1994 recovered objects and a small portion of the hull. Its planks were joined with pegged mortise-and-tenon joints, evidence of skilled shipbuilding as well as trade. The ship's name, exact destination and complete cargo remain unknown. Rather than drawing one certain route, compare this wreck with the atlas's copper complaint and palace records. Each preserves a different moment in the movement of materials, people and obligations.
summary.zh:
安纳托利亚海岸外沉没的一艘船，运载的远不只是完工奢侈品。铜锭和锡锭与玻璃、象牙、琥珀、树脂、食品及制成物并列。这些原料指向尚未完成的劳动：铸造、雕刻、着色及加工。货物让相隔遥远的作坊显露为相互联系的经济的一部分。

1984—1994年的发掘回收了器物及一小部分船体，船板以带木钉的榫接相连，既反映贸易，也反映造船技艺。船名、确切目的地与完整货单仍然不明。将沉船与图集中的铜交易投诉及宫廷记录比较，比绘出一条确定航线更有依据；它们各自保存了材料、人员和责任流动中的不同片刻。

dateNote.en: Approximately the end of the fourteenth century BCE. The 1325–1300 BCE window represents the debated dating summarized by the Nautical Archaeology Digital Library, not a dated voyage log.
dateNote.zh: 约公元前十四世纪末。前1325—前1300年的区间表示航海考古数字图书馆所概括的断代讨论，并非有纪年的航海日志。

sources.title: Uluburun, c.1310 BC
sources.publisher: Carlos de Juan Fuertes, Nautical Archaeology Digital Library
sources.evidenceNote: Summarizes excavation, approximate coordinates, cargo, mortise-and-tenon hull construction and competing chronological approaches, with archaeological bibliography. Unsupported superlatives about earliest ships are omitted.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 概括发掘、约略坐标、货物、榫接船体及断代方法分歧，并附考古文献；未采用最早船舶等绝对化说法。

expansion.sourceReview: Original bilingual synthesis from inspected institutional records, primary documents and specialist research; source-specific claims and limits are retained.

reviewLimit.en: Cargo origins do not establish every port visited. No exact itinerary, captain identity, ethnic crew composition or ship name is reconstructed.
reviewLimit.zh: 货源不能确定所有停靠港；不复原精确行程、船长身份、船员族属或船名。

title.en: Persepolis: feeding an empire one receipt at a time
title.zh: 波斯波利斯：一张张收据维持供给

location.label: Persepolis, central archive of regional transactions

labelI18n.en: Persepolis, central archive of regional transactions
labelI18n.zh: 波斯波利斯，区域交易记录的集中档案地

summary.en:
Imperial administration could take the form of a modest clay receipt. The Persepolis Fortification archive records grain, flour, beer, livestock and other provisions moving through a regional system. Workers and officials received allocations; authorized travelers carried sealed documents indicating what they could obtain along the road. Records of local transactions returned to the central offices, where scribes also assembled longer accounts.

These tablets change the scale at which an empire can be studied. A palace relief displays an ordered world, while an account reveals the repeated work needed to supply it. Most records are in Elamite, showing that Persian imperial government operated through more than one language. The archive offers unusually detailed evidence for this region, but its ration system cannot simply be projected onto every province or equated with modern wages and employment contracts.
summary.zh:
帝国行政也会以一张小小的泥板收据出现。波斯波利斯城防档案记录谷物、面粉、啤酒、牲畜等物资在区域体系内流转。工人与官员领取配给，获准旅行者携带盖印文书，说明途中可以取得的供给。地方交易记录送回中枢，书吏又编成较长时段的账目。

这些泥板改变了研究帝国的尺度。宫殿浮雕展现井然有序的世界，账目却显示维持它所需的重复劳动。多数记录采用埃兰语，说明波斯帝国行政使用的不止一种语言。档案为该区域提供细致证据，但不能把这里的配给方式推广到每个行省，也不能直接等同于现代工资与雇佣合同。

dateNote.en: 509–494 BCE follows the regnal conversion in Encyclopaedia Iranica; the ISAC introduction rounds the archive’s endpoint to 493 BCE. This is the Fortification archive, distinct from the later Treasury tablets.
dateNote.zh: 前509—前494年依《伊朗百科全书》的王年换算；ISAC导言把终点表述为前493年。此处为城防档案，与稍后的国库泥板不同。

sources.title: Persepolis Fortification Tablets
sources.publisher: Richard T. Hallock edition; ISAC, University of Chicago
sources.evidenceNote: Publication introduction explains organized food allocations, sealed travel authorizations and records sent to Persepolis, while cautioning against generalization to the entire empire.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 出版导言说明有组织的食物分配、盖印旅行凭据及送往波斯波利斯的记录，并指出不宜推广至整个帝国。

sources.title: Persepolis Elamite Tablets
sources.evidenceNote: Distinguishes Fortification and Treasury archives, dates the former 509–494 BCE, and explains regional receipts, aggregated accounts and food transfers.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 区分城防与国库档案，将前者定为前509—前494年，说明区域收据、汇总账目与食物调拨。

expansion.sourceReview: Original bilingual synthesis from inspected institutional records, primary documents and specialist research; source-specific claims and limits are retained.

reviewLimit.en: Ration categories alone do not establish modern employment status or prove a uniform imperial economy. No assertion of equal pay or paid maternity leave is made.
reviewLimit.zh: 配给分类本身不能确定现代意义的雇佣身份，也不能证明帝国经济划一；不据此声称同工同酬或带薪产假。

title.en: Bukhara suzani: joining a family’s work
title.zh: 布哈拉苏扎尼：拼合家人的针线

labelI18n.zh: 所归属的制作地区布哈拉

summary.en:
The seams in a suzani can reveal how a household organized work. A specialist drew a design across loosely joined fabric strips; women then separated the strips, embroidered them and brought the completed sections together. Slight changes of color or alignment record that shared process. Such embroidered covers furnished homes and formed part of marriage preparations, displaying both skill and a family's resources.

An early nineteenth-century cover attributed to Bukhara provides one example, not a template for every Central Asian household. Research with Bukharan Jewish families also places suzani within Muslim and Jewish histories and follows textiles carried into migration. Read it beside the atlas's Bukhara court sequence: dynasties changed, while domestic objects held other kinds of memory. A border, a join or a repaired section may ask a historical question that a royal chronology never poses.
summary.zh:
苏扎尼绣品的接缝可以显示家人怎样安排劳动。专业画样者先在暂时拼合的布条上描图，女子再拆开各条，分别刺绣，最后把成品合在一起。颜色或位置的细小差异留下了协作过程。这些绣盖装点住宅，也用于婚姻准备，展示技艺与家庭资源。

一件归于布哈拉的十九世纪早期绣盖提供了实例，却不能代表所有中亚家庭。对布哈拉犹太家庭的研究，还把苏扎尼放入穆斯林与犹太社群的历史，并追踪迁移中随身带走的织物。将它与布哈拉宫廷变迁并读，可以看到王朝之外的记忆。边饰、接缝或补缀所引出的历史问题，往往不会出现在君王年表中。

dateNote.en: 1800–1830 is an approximate display window for the catalogue’s “early nineteenth century.” Bukhara is an attribution; migration belongs to later reception and use, not this object’s production date.
dateNote.zh: 1800—1830年为目录“十九世纪早期”的约略显示区间。布哈拉为归属判断；迁移属于后来的使用与接受史，并非此件制作年代。

sources.title: Cover, 21.114.3
sources.evidenceNote: Supports early nineteenth-century dating, attribution to Bukhara, design across separate strips and women’s collaborative embroidery. The object medium is silk on linen; the general cotton description is not imposed on this example.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 支持十九世纪早期、归于布哈拉、分条画样及女子协作刺绣；此件材质为丝绣于亚麻底，不将概述中的棉底强加于此件。

sources.title: Suzani Vernacular: Technique and Design in the Central Asian Dowry Embroideries
sources.publisher: Angela Izrailova, Textile Society of America; University of Nebraska repository
sources.evidenceNote: Author’s research introduction identifies Muslim and Jewish women’s production, household uses and textiles carried by late twentieth-century Bukharan Jewish migrants. Only the accessible introduction is used.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 作者研究导言确认穆斯林与犹太女子制作、家庭用途及二十世纪晚期布哈拉犹太移民携带织物；仅使用可读导言。

expansion.sourceReview: Original bilingual synthesis from inspected institutional records, primary documents and specialist research; source-specific claims and limits are retained.

reviewLimit.en: The anonymous object is not assigned a bride, named embroiderer or migration journey. Household cooperation is interpreted from the documented production method.
reviewLimit.zh: 不为匿名器物指定新娘、具名绣者或迁移行程；家庭协作据有记录的制作方法解释。

title.en: Ferghana ikat: the pattern begins before the loom
title.zh: 费尔干纳伊卡特：织机之前已有图案

location.label: Ferghana Valley, textile production region; approximate

labelI18n.en: Ferghana Valley, textile production region; approximate
labelI18n.zh: 费尔干纳谷地织物产区；约指

summary.en:
Ikat reverses a familiar expectation: the pattern is planned on threads before they become cloth. Workers bind selected areas of yarn to resist dye, then arrange and weave the colored threads. A Ferghana wall hanging dated 1850–1875 combines an ikat-dyed silk warp with an undyed cotton weft. Its soft-edged forms emerge from that coordinated preparation.

Production connected people who raised silkworms, reeled fiber, tied and dyed yarn, wove fabric and finished its surface. Museum research describes specializations across gender and community in Central Asian towns; these were historical working arrangements, not fixed natural roles. Robes and hangings also displayed status and furnished celebrations. Linking this object to Kokand and Bukhara adds workshops and households to histories usually organized around khans, conquest and borders.
summary.zh:
伊卡特颠倒了人们熟悉的顺序：线还没有成为布，图案已经开始安排。工人扎住纱线的指定部分以防染，再整理、织合染好的经线。一件定于1850—1875年的费尔干纳挂毯，采用扎染丝经与未染棉纬，边缘柔和的形状来自协调过的准备工作。

制作连接养蚕、缫丝、扎线、染色、织造和整理表面的劳动者。博物馆研究记述中亚城市中不同性别与社群的分工，它们是历史中的工作安排，并非天然不变的角色。袍服与挂毯也表现身份，装点节庆。把此件与浩罕、布哈拉联系起来，便能在以汗王、征服和边界编排的历史中加入作坊与家庭。

dateNote.en: 1850–1875 is the catalogue date of Smithsonian S2006.8. The valley marker is representative and does not identify a particular workshop or the makers’ later movements.
dateNote.zh: 1850—1875年为史密森学会S2006.8号器物的目录断代；谷地地图点仅作示意，不指认具体作坊或制作者后来的流动。

sources.title: Wall hanging, S2006.8
sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art
sources.evidenceNote: Supports Ferghana attribution, 1850–1875, silk warp/cotton weft, resist-dyeing before weaving, social uses and several production specializations. The label’s broad empire chronology is not reused.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 支持费尔干纳归属、1850—1875年、丝经棉纬、织前防染、社会用途及制作分工；未采用标签中过于概括的帝国年代叙事。

expansion.sourceReview: Original bilingual synthesis from inspected institutional records, primary documents and specialist research; source-specific claims and limits are retained.

reviewLimit.en: Ethnic and gender specializations are the museum’s regional historical description, not the documented identity of this object’s unknown makers.
reviewLimit.zh: 族群与性别分工是博物馆对区域历史的概述，不是此匿名器物制作者已确定的身份。

title.en: Cibali: the workers behind the factory photograph
title.zh: 吉巴利：工厂照片背后的劳动者

labelI18n.zh: 伊斯坦布尔吉巴利烟草厂

summary.en:
Photographs of the Cibali tobacco factory show rows of women packing tobacco and rolling cigarettes. The work demanded precision, although employers and observers often categorized women's tasks as unskilled. Studying the photographs beside factory documents brings discipline, gender and pay into the story of Ottoman industrial change.

The factory began operating for the tobacco Régie in 1884. In 1904, workers protesting withheld payments marched to its headquarters; women participated alongside men. The settlement divided workers by religious community, while dismissal and police action followed. Names preserved in the investigation, including Mari Behar and Raşel Eskinazi, interrupt the anonymity of the workshop image. Their history connects imperial finance to repeated hand movements, wages and collective action. The photograph's ordered rows did not mean that the people sitting in them accepted their conditions.
summary.zh:
吉巴利烟草厂的照片里，成排女子包装烟叶、卷制香烟。这些工作要求精确，雇主和观察者却常把女子任务列为非技术劳动。把照片与工厂文书并读，便能在奥斯曼工业变化中看到纪律、性别与工资。

该厂于1884年开始为烟草专卖公司经营。1904年，工人为被扣留的款项抗议，游行到公司总部，女子与男子共同参与。最后的处理按宗教社群区别对待，随后还有解雇与警察追查。调查保存的玛丽·贝哈尔、拉谢尔·埃斯基纳齐等姓名，打破了工坊图像中的匿名状态。这段历史把帝国财政与重复的手部劳动、报酬及集体行动相连。照片中整齐的座位，并不意味着坐在那里的人接受工作条件。

dateNote.en: Focus: the factory’s opening in 1884 through the documented 1904 wage protest. Later nationalization and reuse of the building are outside this story’s time window.
dateNote.zh: 重点为1884年开厂至有文献记录的1904年工资抗议；后来的国有化与建筑改用不属于本篇时段。

sources.title: Tobacco Factory
sources.evidenceNote: Museum history dates the Régie factory’s operation to 1884 and describes its institutional setting. The opening anecdote presented as hearsay is not used.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 馆方历史将专卖公司工厂运营定在1884年，说明制度背景；未采用开篇以传闻方式呈现的故事。

sources.title: Gendering Ottoman Labor History: The Cibali Régie Factory in the Early Twentieth Century
sources.publisher: Gülhan Balsoy, International Review of Social History
sources.evidenceNote: The photograph analysis and archival 1904 protest section support task classifications, women’s participation, differential settlement and the named women. No medical statistics or inferred religious identity from clothing are reused.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 照片分析及1904年抗议档案节支持工种分类、女子参与、差别处理与具名女子；未采用医学统计或根据衣着推定宗教身份。

expansion.sourceReview: Original bilingual synthesis from inspected institutional records, primary documents and specialist research; source-specific claims and limits are retained.

reviewLimit.en: The article identifies named participants through police records. It does not allow assigning a name to a particular face in a factory photograph.
reviewLimit.zh: 文章通过警察记录识别参与者，不能据此把姓名指定给工厂照片中的某张面孔。

title.en: Bethlehem embroidery: stitches, repairs and visitors
title.zh: 伯利恒刺绣：针脚、修补与来客

labelI18n.zh: 制衣与刺绣所在的伯利恒

summary.en:
A dress preserves decisions made long after its first stitches. A nineteenth-century Bethlehem thobe in the Palestinian Museum combines handwoven fabric, metallic and silk embroidery, added sections and patches. Its chest panel uses tahriri, or couching: threads are laid along the surface and secured in place. Following those joins makes repair part of the object's history.

Bethlehem women developed a recognizable embroidery style, while dresses and embroidered souvenirs connected local work with pilgrims and wider markets. Cloth could therefore express belonging and also circulate beyond the town. Read this object beside the atlas's Ottoman and mandate histories to see a different scale of continuity. The surviving garment cannot identify every maker or wearer, but it records skill, adaptation and continued use in ways that a change of government cannot summarize.
summary.zh:
一件衣服保存的决定，可能远晚于最初几针。巴勒斯坦博物馆收藏的一件十九世纪伯利恒长袍，将手织布、金属线与丝线刺绣、添接布块和补丁组合在一起。胸片使用塔赫里里盘金式钉线绣，将线铺在表面再固定。沿着接缝阅读，修补便成为器物历史的一部分。

伯利恒女子发展出有辨识度的刺绣风格，服装与刺绣纪念品又把本地劳动同朝圣者及更广市场连接起来。布料既能表现归属，也能流通到城镇之外。将此件与奥斯曼及委任统治历史并读，可看到另一尺度的延续。衣服不能识别每位制作者或穿用者，却以政权更替无法概括的方式，记录技艺、调整与持续使用。

dateNote.en: About 1850–1900 follows the Palestinian Museum’s date for object 0002.01.0082. The broader souvenir market is documented for the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.
dateNote.zh: 约1850—1900年依巴勒斯坦博物馆0002.01.0082号器物断代；较广的纪念品市场有十九世纪晚期至二十世纪早期的记录。

sources.title: Bethlehem thobe, 0002.01.0082
sources.evidenceNote: The collection record supplies c.1850–1900, handloom fabric, couching, added back cloth and multiple patches. A search-result mourning-use description absent from the opened record is not adopted.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 馆藏条目提供约1850—1900年、手织布、钉线绣、背部添布与多处补缀；未采用搜索摘要中、已打开条目未见的丧服说法。

sources.title: Reading the History of Bethlehem through Embroidery
sources.evidenceNote: Museum lecture description supports women’s local style and embroidered souvenirs sold to pilgrims; it does not trace this specific garment’s ownership.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 博物馆讲座说明支持女子本地风格及售予朝圣者的刺绣纪念品，不追溯此件具体衣物的所有权。

expansion.sourceReview: Original bilingual synthesis from inspected institutional records, primary documents and specialist research; source-specific claims and limits are retained.

reviewLimit.en: The garment’s alterations are observable catalogue evidence. Its individual maker, wearer, religion and political views are not inferred from regional motifs.
reviewLimit.zh: 衣物改动来自目录实物描述，不从区域纹样推定个人制作者、穿用者、宗教或政治观点。

title.en: An invitation at Vindolanda: two hands, one friendship
title.zh: 文多兰达的请柬：两种笔迹，一段友谊

location.label: Vindolanda, the recipient’s fort and the tablet’s findspot

labelI18n.en: Vindolanda, the recipient’s fort and the tablet’s findspot
labelI18n.zh: 收信人所在的文多兰达军堡，也是木牍出土地

summary.en:
Claudia Severa wanted Sulpicia Lepidina to come to her birthday celebration on 11 September. Her invitation survives on a thin wooden tablet found at Vindolanda, a Roman fort in northern Britain. Its message reaches beyond an official military world: a friend's presence would make the day happier, and greetings pass between the two households.

Two hands made the letter. The main message has an elegant, practiced script; Severa added the affectionate closing herself, according to the editors' analysis. That change of handwriting brings the writer into view without requiring a portrait. The tablet belongs to a context dated 97–105 CE, although its particular year is unknown. Beside accounts of Roman government and citizenship, it preserves the social work of friendship among women connected to the frontier's military households.
summary.zh:
克劳迪娅·塞韦拉希望苏尔皮基娅·莱皮迪娜来参加9月11日的生日聚会。她的邀请保存在一枚薄木牍上，出土于不列颠北部的罗马军堡文多兰达。文字把人带到军务之外：朋友到场，会让这一天更愉快，两家人也相互致意。

信中可以辨出两种笔迹。正文书写娴熟；根据整理者的分析，塞韦拉亲手补上亲昵的结尾。笔迹的变化无需肖像，也让写信者变得可见。木牍所属的考古层位被定于公元97—105年，但具体写于哪一年尚不可知。与罗马政权和公民权的记述并读，它保存了边疆军事家庭中女子经营友谊的日常。

dateNote.en: 97–105 CE is the archaeological context range. The text supplies 11 September for the birthday, not a uniquely recoverable year; the map marks the recipient’s fort and findspot.
dateNote.zh: 公元97—105年是考古层位年代。正文给出生日为9月11日，不能确定唯一年份；地图标记收信人所在军堡与出土地。

sources.title: Tab. Vindol. 291: Birthday Invitation of Sulpicia Lepidina
sources.publisher: Roman Inscriptions of Britain, edited Vindolanda tablets
sources.evidenceNote: The edition, translation and palaeographic commentary establish the senders, birthday, wooden medium, two hands, Severa’s closing and context date 97–105.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 校本、译文及笔迹注释支持写信人与收信人、生日、木质载体、两种笔迹、塞韦拉结尾及97—105年层位。

expansion.sourceReview: Original bilingual synthesis from inspected institutional records, primary documents and specialist research; source-specific claims and limits are retained.

reviewLimit.en: The affectionate address “sister” is not evidence of biological kinship. This elite household letter does not establish a general literacy rate or the invitation’s precise place of composition.
reviewLimit.zh: 亲昵称呼“姐妹”不能证明血缘关系。这封上层家庭书信不能确定普遍识字率，也不能确定写信的准确地点。

title.en: Onfim’s bark: practice, play and medieval literacy
title.zh: 昂菲姆的树皮：练习、游戏与中世纪书写

location.label: Novgorod, where Onfim’s birch-bark exercises were found

labelI18n.en: Novgorod, where Onfim’s birch-bark exercises were found
labelI18n.zh: 昂菲姆树皮习作的发现地诺夫哥罗德

summary.en:
A rider thrusts a spear toward a fallen opponent, and the name Onfim appears nearby. Scratched into birch bark in thirteenth-century Novgorod, the drawing belongs to a group of a child's writing exercises. Other pieces carry alphabets, syllables, church texts and the formulas used to begin letters. The collection places imaginative play beside the repetitive work of learning to write.

Museum researchers interpret the rider as Onfim picturing himself as a hero. The drawing allows that reading without revealing everything about its maker's life. The exercises also move between bookish letter forms and forms used in ordinary notes. Together they make medieval literacy tangible: a surface, a pointed tool, practiced signs and a child's choices. They offer a different entry into the period from rulers, trading towns or universities.
summary.zh:
骑马者把长矛指向倒下的对手，旁边写着“昂菲姆”。这幅刻在桦树皮上的画来自十三世纪诺夫哥罗德，属于一组儿童习作。其他树皮写有字母、音节、教会文本及书信开头的套语，让想象游戏与反复练字出现在同一组材料里。

博物馆研究者将骑马者解释为昂菲姆想象中的英雄自画像。这种解读有根据，却不足以还原孩子的全部生活。习作还涉及书面语字形与日常记录字形。把这些材料放在一起，中世纪识字便成为具体经验：书写表面、尖头工具、练过的符号，以及孩子自己的选择。与君主、贸易城市或大学相比，它们提供了另一种进入那个时代的方式。

dateNote.en: 1240–1260 is the museum catalogue’s dating of the birch-bark object, not Onfim’s lifespan or a precisely dated school term.
dateNote.zh: 1240—1260年为博物馆对树皮实物的断代，不是昂菲姆生卒年或精确学期。

sources.title: Birch bark manuscript of a boy named Onfim
sources.publisher: State Historical Museum collection, ARTEFACT museum portal
sources.evidenceNote: Provides Novgorod, 1240–1260, scratched birch bark, the signed rider, exercise contents and bookish/vernacular letter forms. The self-portrait is an interpretation.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 提供诺夫哥罗德、1240—1260年、桦树皮刻写、署名骑马者、习作内容及书面与日常字形；自画像属于解释。

expansion.sourceReview: Original bilingual synthesis from inspected institutional records, primary documents and specialist research; source-specific claims and limits are retained.

reviewLimit.en: No exact age, family occupation or school is assigned. A copied debt-collection formula is not treated as proof that the child conducted that transaction.
reviewLimit.zh: 不指定确切年龄、家庭职业或学校；抄写的催债套语不被当作孩子实际办理此交易的证明。

title.en: Aldus and Griffo: classics designed to be carried
title.zh: 阿尔杜斯与格里福：可以随身携带的古典作品

location.label: Venice, workshop setting of the Aldine press

labelI18n.en: Venice, workshop setting of the Aldine press
labelI18n.zh: 阿尔杜斯印刷坊所在的威尼斯

summary.en:
A reader could carry a classical text in a smaller book. In 1501, Aldus Manutius's Venetian press began issuing portable editions, including Virgil in April and Horace in May. The Virgil was the first complete book printed in the new italic type. Its letter shapes borrowed from humanist handwriting, giving printed pages something of a manuscript's appearance.

That design depended on Francesco Griffo, who cut the type. Examination of surviving copies shows that the letterforms continued to change while the Virgil was being printed. Publisher, type cutter and press workers were making a new reading object together. Placed after Gutenberg in the atlas, this story follows a different question: once books could be multiplied, how should they look and fit into a reader's life? Portability and typography were choices made through skilled work.
summary.zh:
读者可以把古典作品装进一本较小的书随身携带。1501年，阿尔杜斯·马努提乌斯的威尼斯印刷坊开始推出便携版本，其中有四月的维吉尔和五月的贺拉斯。维吉尔集是第一部全书采用新斜体字印刷的书，字形借鉴人文主义者的手写体，让印页带有手稿的观感。

这种设计依赖雕刻字模的弗朗切斯科·格里福。对传世版本的比较表明，维吉尔集仍在印刷时，字形还在继续调整。出版者、刻字者与印工共同制作新的阅读物件。把本篇接在古腾堡之后，可以追问另一个问题：书籍能够成批印制以后，应当怎样呈现，又怎样进入读者生活？便携性与字体，都是通过熟练劳动做出的选择。

dateNote.en: 1501 marks the Virgil and Horace editions and the start of the portable series. Italic had already appeared in a few printed words in 1500; no claim of invention in a single year is made.
dateNote.zh: 1501年标记维吉尔、贺拉斯版本及便携系列的开端。1500年已有少量斜体印字，不把发明归为单一年份。

sources.title: Pressing Business: Aldus Manutius exhibition
sources.evidenceNote: Exhibited copies establish April/May 1501, Griffo’s type cutting, manuscript models and refinement during printing. The exhibition rejects the claim that italic necessarily saved paper and lowered costs.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 展出实物支持1501年四、五月、格里福刻字、手写体范本及印制中调整；展览否定斜体必然省纸降价的说法。

sources.title: Aldus Manutius and Early Medical Humanist Publishing
sources.publisher: Michael North, National Library of Medicine
sources.evidenceNote: The rare-books curator dates the introduction of portable classical editions to 1501. Its general attribution of typography to Aldus is qualified by the Grolier exhibition’s evidence for Griffo.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 善本馆员将便携古典版本的推出定于1501年；其概括归功于阿尔杜斯的字体说明，以格罗利尔展览关于格里福的证据补充。

expansion.sourceReview: Original bilingual synthesis from inspected institutional records, primary documents and specialist research; source-specific claims and limits are retained.

reviewLimit.en: Small format is not evidence that every reader could afford these books. Italic’s appearance is distinguished from unsupported claims that it automatically reduced cost.
reviewLimit.zh: 小开本不等于人人买得起；斜体的外观与“必然降低成本”的无据说法分开。

title.en: Lyon’s silk workers: who sets the price of work?
title.zh: 里昂丝织工：谁来定劳动的价格？

location.label: Croix-Rousse, Lyon, center of the silk workers’ movement

labelI18n.en: Croix-Rousse, Lyon, center of the silk workers’ movement
labelI18n.zh: 里昂红十字山，丝织工运动中心

summary.en:
Silk could command a high price while the people weaving it struggled over their share. In autumn 1831, Lyon's canuts sought a higher payment tariff from merchant manufacturers. The prefect mediated an agreement in October, but manufacturers refused to apply it. A dispute over rates moved from negotiation into the streets.

In November, workers descended from the Croix-Rousse weaving district and took control of the city after armed clashes. Government troops returned on 3 December; the workers had not secured the tariff they sought. The episode exposes a question behind an elegant fabric: who can decide what skilled work is worth, and who can enforce that decision? Read beside Britain's factory legislation and later labor movements, it shows a struggle over bargaining power within a specialized urban trade.
summary.zh:
丝绸可以售价高昂，织造者却仍要争取自己的报酬。1831年秋，里昂的卡尼丝织工要求商人制造商提高计件工价。省长在十月促成协议，但制造商拒绝执行。关于工价的争执从谈判桌转向街头。

十一月，工人从红十字山织造区下山，在武装冲突后控制城市。政府军于12月3日返回，工人并未获得所要求的工价标准。这段经历揭示华美织物背后的问题：谁能决定熟练劳动值多少钱，又由谁保证决定得到执行？与英国工厂立法和后来的劳动运动并读，可以看到专业化城市行业中对议价权的争夺。

dateNote.en: This record concerns the 1831 tariff dispute and revolt. The separate 1834 uprising is not folded into the same event.
dateNote.zh: 本条聚焦1831年工价争议与起义，不将另一次1834年起义并入同一事件。

sources.title: Les origines de la révolte de 1831
sources.evidenceNote: Supports the tariff demand, October agreement, non-application, November occupation and 3 December return of troops. Casualty totals and the page’s claim of no repression are not adopted.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 支持工价诉求、十月协议、未执行、十一月占领及12月3日军队返回；未采用伤亡总数或该页“没有镇压”的概括。

sources.title: Revivez la révolte des canuts à Gadagne
sources.evidenceNote: Confirms the refusal to implement a minimum tariff, the Croix-Rousse setting and December troop return; its economic and day-by-day details are not imposed where accounts diverge.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 确认拒绝最低工价、红十字山背景及十二月军队返回；不同记述有出入的经济与逐日细节未强行统一。

expansion.sourceReview: Original bilingual synthesis from inspected institutional records, primary documents and specialist research; source-specific claims and limits are retained.

reviewLimit.en: Institutional accounts differ on some immediate chronology and repression. The shared documented sequence is retained without a casualty estimate or a uniform wage-cut percentage.
reviewLimit.zh: 机构记述对部分直接时序与镇压情况有出入；保留共同支持的事件顺序，不列伤亡估计或统一减薪比例。

title.en: Oneg Shabbat: making an archive under persecution
title.zh: 安息日之乐：迫害下建立档案

labelI18n.zh: 原华沙犹太隔离区；代表位置

summary.en:
A school essay, an official order and a refugee's account could each preserve a different part of life under Nazi German occupation. In the Warsaw ghetto, historian Emanuel Ringelblum organized Oneg Shabbat, a clandestine group that gathered documents and commissioned testimony. Teachers wrote about education while children supplied their own perspectives. Welfare work brought collectors into contact with refugees and news from other Jewish communities.

As evidence of mass murder arrived, the group also gathered and transmitted information about deportations and killing. Members buried collections in metal boxes and milk cans during 1942–1943. Two sections were recovered after the war, in 1946 and 1950. The archive lets us hear people describing conditions while they were living through them. Its creation was collective work under persecution; its survival was incomplete, as were the lives and communities it recorded.
summary.zh:
一篇学生作文、一份官方命令和一位难民的叙述，都可能保存纳粹德国占领下生活的不同部分。在华沙犹太隔离区，历史学家埃马努埃尔·林格尔布鲁姆组织秘密团体“安息日之乐”，收集文书并约请人们留下见证。教师写教育状况，孩子也提供自己的视角。救济工作让收集者接触难民，并获得其他犹太社区的消息。

随着大规模杀戮的证据传来，团体也收集、传递关于驱逐与屠杀的信息。成员在1942—1943年将材料装入金属箱和奶罐埋藏。战后于1946年和1950年找回两部分。这批档案让人听到亲历者在事情发生时怎样描述处境。建立档案是迫害中的共同劳动；保存下来的材料并不完整，而它所记录的人与社区也遭到摧毁。

dateNote.en: 1940–1943 focuses on the organized ghetto archive and its wartime concealment. Ringelblum’s earlier note taking began in 1939; recovery in 1946 and 1950 is a later history.
dateNote.zh: 1940—1943年聚焦隔离区有组织的档案工作及战时埋藏。林格尔布鲁姆早在1939年已开始记录；1946与1950年的发掘属于后续历史。

sources.title: The Oneg Shabbat Archives: overview
sources.evidenceNote: The overview documents diverse contributors, teachers and children, refugee contacts, official papers, reporting on murder and burial in 1942–1943. No uniform container count is asserted.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 概述记载多元参与者、师生、难民接触、官方文件、屠杀报告及1942—1943年埋藏；不采用统一容器数量。

sources.title: In Memoriam: Emanuel Ringelblum
sources.publisher: American Jewish Joint Distribution Committee Archives
sources.evidenceNote: Distinguishes recording begun in 1939 from expansion after the ghetto’s establishment in 1940; documents welfare networks, metal boxes/milk cans and recovery in 1946 and 1950.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 区分1939年开始记录与1940年隔离区建立后的扩充；说明救济网络、金属箱和奶罐及1946、1950年发现。

expansion.sourceReview: Original bilingual synthesis from inspected institutional records, primary documents and specialist research; source-specific claims and limits are retained.

reviewLimit.en: The archive is not complete, and the map does not claim to identify a burial spot. The story distinguishes contemporary testimony, deliberate collection and later recovery.
reviewLimit.zh: 档案并不完整，地图不声称标出埋藏点；区分当时见证、主动搜集与后来的发现。

title.en: Grunwick: dignity and the limits of solidarity
title.zh: 格伦维克：尊严与团结的限度

location.label: Willesden and Dollis Hill, London, Grunwick dispute setting

labelI18n.en: Willesden and Dollis Hill, London, Grunwick dispute setting
labelI18n.zh: 伦敦威尔斯登与多利斯山，格伦维克争议发生地

summary.en:
Holiday photographs passed through the hands of workers at Grunwick's film-processing factory in London. In August 1976, employees walked out over low pay, racism, degrading conditions and the lack of union recognition. Many were recently settled migrants, and most were women of South Asian heritage. Jayaben Desai became a leading voice of the strike.

The campaign brought other unions, anti-racist groups and feminist supporters to the picket line. Postal workers also interrupted deliveries to a business that depended on customers sending film. Yet public solidarity did not secure the strikers' demands. By the dispute's end in 1978, management had neither reinstated them nor recognized their union, and major union bodies had withdrawn support. This is a history of women and migrant workers organizing on their own behalf, with an outcome that prevents an easy story of inevitable progress.
summary.zh:
度假照片在伦敦格伦维克冲印厂经过工人的双手。1976年八月，雇员因低薪、种族歧视、羞辱性的工作条件及工会不获承认而罢工。许多人是新近定居的移民，多数为南亚裔女子。贾亚本·德赛成为罢工的主要发言者。

行动把其他工会、反种族歧视团体和女性主义支持者带到纠察线。邮政工人也中断送件，影响这家依赖顾客邮寄胶卷的企业。然而公众支持并未实现罢工者诉求。到1978年争议结束，资方既没有让他们复职，也没有承认工会，主要工会组织已经撤回支持。这是一段女子与移民工人为自己组织行动的历史，其结果无法写成必然进步的简单故事。

dateNote.en: 1976–1978 follows the museum’s dispute chronology. August 1976 marks the initial walkout; the endpoint records defeat rather than a settlement granting recognition.
dateNote.zh: 1976—1978年依据博物馆争议纪年。1976年八月为最初罢工，终点代表失败，而非获得承认的和解。

sources.title: The Grunwick strike, 1976–1978
sources.evidenceNote: Supports the factory work, August walkout, Desai, migrant and women workers, union/public/postal solidarity, withdrawal of support and failure to secure reinstatement or recognition.
sources.evidenceNoteZh: 支持工厂业务、八月罢工、德赛、移民与女工、工会公众及邮政支持、撤回支持及未获复职或承认。

expansion.sourceReview: Original bilingual synthesis from inspected institutional records, primary documents and specialist research; source-specific claims and limits are retained.

reviewLimit.en: No participant’s origin is inferred from appearance. The museum’s outcome is retained; the strike is not presented as winning recognition or causing all subsequent labor reforms.
reviewLimit.zh: 不从外貌推断参与者出身。保留博物馆记述的结果，不将罢工写成赢得承认或造成此后所有劳动改革。
